summary: Intro discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Halcyon evaluating hosted for quick time-to-first-token, asking about free credits, security posture, and path to Dedicated/Private for production. Next: share quickstart, security docs, run benchmark & schedule SE deep-dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Halcyon Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Priya Singh (Platform Eng)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya's our SE and she'll cover technical questions.
00:12 Alicia Gomez: Hi all, Alicia here, head of ML at Halcyon. We're evaluating provider for a self-serve API integration and want to understand time to first token and what a PLG quickstart would look like.
00:25 Tom Reynolds: Tom, CTO. We care about security and how we scale when this moves to prod  



00:34 Priya Nair: Great, thanks. We'll walk through the quickstart flow, free credits, and then talk about hosted vs dedicated vs private. Feel free to interrupt.
00:44 Jordan Lee: First question  

what are you trying to build in the first 90 days?
00:49 Alicia Gomez: We want an in-app assistant for our analytics product: short chat completions, embeddings for search, and a rerank step. Low latency matters for the UI, ideally sub 300ms on single-turn completions, but we're flexible early on.
01:05 Priya Singh: From infra side we prefer a managed hosted API to move fast, but will likely want Dedicated or Private once we hit certain traffic or data retention constraints. We need SSO and audit logs.
01:18 Priya Nair: Makes sense. Quickstart: Redwood PLG flow gets you an API key, quickstart SDK snippets in JS/Python, and a sandbox with free credits. Time-to-first-token is usually under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart and install the SDK. We also provide a sample app and Postman collection.
01:38 Tom Reynolds: Free credits 

how much and are they tied to a trial org? Can multiple engineers use them?
01:45 Jordan Lee: We issue trial credits attached to a trial org. You can invite your engineers, and there are role-based invites. Credits are typically enough for several thousand tokens  






















02:03 Alicia Gomez: Is there a sandbox model or is it the same models as production?
02:09 Priya Nair: The quickstart exposes our hosted model catalog  





02:25 Tom Reynolds: On benchmarking  



02:31 Priya Nair: Yes, Priya will share a short benchmark checklist with suggested prompt sets, concurrency patterns, and how to measure p95 and throughput. We also provide sample curl and SDK scripts.
02:45 Jordan Lee: I want to flag hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to get started and lowest friction; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulated workloads with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integration.
02:59 Alicia Gomez: For us, data residency and KMS are musts if we store user PII or customer data. How does Redwood handle encryption and KMS?
03:07 Priya Nair: We integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated setups; hosted supports envelope encryption and we can discuss bring-your-own-key options for enterprise. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and the security pack.
03:20 Tom Reynolds: Do you do per-route RBAC and audit logs? We need traceability for internal audits.
03:26 Priya Nair: Yes, the console has per-route access controls, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs. For Private installs we can provide logs to your SIEM.
03:35 Alicia Gomez: Latency targets 

you mentioned sub 300ms. How do you meet that with larger contexts or streaming?
03:42 Priya Nair: Short completions on optimized models are often under 200-300ms on good networking and single-token generation. Longer contexts or streaming will increase latency, but we do KV cache, continuous batching, and optimized kernels. In Dedicated you can pin GPUs and get consistent p95s.
03:58 Priya Singh: Are there autoscaling options for Dedicated? We prefer predictability but want burst handling.
04:04 Jordan Lee: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity options. We also have failover policies 


if Dedicated capacity is full we can fallback to a compatible hosted variant depending on your policy.
04:15 Alicia Gomez: Any limitations around embeddings throughput? We're planning a nightly batch of embeddings for indexing.
04:21 Priya Nair: For batch embeddings we recommend using larger-batch endpoints or a dedicated GPU pool. The Optimize toolkit will recommend batching/quantization profiles to reduce unit cost.
04:33 Tom Reynolds: Compliance 


do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM?
04:37 Priya Nair: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning for enterprise orgs; we'll include setup docs in the security pack.
04:45 Alicia Gomez: Pricing 

what's the PLG pricing vs Dedicated commit? High-level numbers are fine for now.
04:50 Jordan Lee: For PLG we have usage-based pricing per token and embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits which lowers unit cost. We'll send a simple comparison in the follow-up.
05:01 Tom Reynolds: For the quickstart

what's the support level? Chat or email?
05:05 Jordan Lee: Self-serve docs + community support, and you get access to a solutions rep during the trial. If you sign a Dedicated or Private contract we provide an onboarding SE and SLA-backed support.
05:14 Priya Singh: I have a question 

can we route requests by region to keep data in EU?
05:20 Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing supports region preferences and policy-based routing. For strict data residency you'd use Private or a dedicated region in our hosting.
05:31 Alicia Gomez: About the quickstart, can we get a demo of the sample app and how tokens show up in the console?
05:36 Jordan Lee: Absolutely 

we'll include a short recorded quickstart demo and can do a live 15-30 minute walk-through.
05:45 Tom Reynolds: If we hit production scale, what's the migration path from hosted to Dedicated? Is it seamless?
05:52 Priya Nair: It's designed to be smooth 


You can pin model versions and do canary deploys; we handle routing to Dedicated capacity once provisioned. There are infra steps (tenant mapping, network setup) but API code doesn't change.
06:10 Alicia Gomez: Any gotchas around inference cost when moving from open models to Redwood-verified opt models?
06:15 Priya Nair: Costs vary by model and quantization. Optimize suggests quant profiles and model variants tuned for latency/cost. We'll include recommended configs for your workload after you run the benchmark.
06:28 Jordan Lee: Quick pause 

Priya, can you highlight the quickstart steps we expect Halcyon to run in the next week?
06:33 Priya Nair: Sure: 1) Sign up for trial org and invite engineers; 2) Run quickstart sample app and get first token; 3) Run benchmark checklist (we'll provide); 4) Share results and decide if Dedicated/Private needed. Most teams get to first token in 5-10 minutes if they have network egress configured.
06:52 Priya Singh: Network egress 

anything special on our side? We use a strict proxy egress policy.
06:57 Priya Nair: You may need to allow our API endpoints or use a proxy allowlist. For Private you can keep traffic inside VPC. We'll note endpoints in the follow-up.
07:07 Tom Reynolds: How do you handle model updates or regression detection? We need quality monitoring.
07:14 Priya Nair: Redwood Optimize ties model/quant changes to prompt sets and evals. We offer alerts for quality regressions and per-route performance dashboards.
07:25 Alicia Gomez: For the free credits can we allocate some to a CI job to run nightly smoke checks?
07:30 Jordan Lee: Yes, you can use credits programmatically, but there are fair-use limits. We'll call out best practices for CI usage.
07:39 Tom Reynolds: Any references or customers similar to us that used PLG and then moved to Dedicated?
07:44 Jordan Lee: We have a few mid-market analytics customers who started on PLG quickstart and moved to Dedicated once they hit predictable throughput; we'll include anonymized case notes in the follow-up.
07:54 Alicia Gomez: Ok great. Can you also surface the security questionnaire and SOC2 report?
07:58 Priya Nain: Yes, security pack and SOC2 will be shared. For Private we can also detail KMS/HSM integration and audit log delivery.
08:07 Jordan Lee: Any other blockers on your side for starting the quickstart?
08:11 Priya Singh: Mainly egress allowlist and confirming the engineers to invite. We'll confirm names after the call.
08:18 Alicia Gomez: Timeline 

we'd like to have a quick prototype in two weeks and evaluate Dedicated in Q1.
08:23 Jordan Lee: Sounds reasonable. We'll coordinate timelines with SE for a follow-up demo.
08:28 Priya Nair: I'll schedule the technical demo and prep a benchmark checklist tailored to your prompts.
08:34 Jordan Lee: Alright let's recap actions.
08:37 Jordan Lee: Action recap: Jordan to send quickstart + free credits guide and recorded demo; Priya (Redwood) to send benchmark checklist and security pack; Halcyon to provision trial org and invite Redwood and run basic benchmark; schedule SE deep-dive for private/dedicated options.
08:58 Tom Reynolds: Cool. One last quick question 

is there a public status page and SLAs for hosted?
09:03 Priya Nair: Yes we have a public status page; SLAs apply to Dedicated. Hosted has best-effort uptime and we publish performance profiles. We'll include links.
09:12 Alicia Gomez: Thanks everyone. We'll look for the follow-up and get the trial running.
09:16 Jordan Lee: Thanks all, talk soon.

End: 2026-12-06 15:42 UTC

Notes: Transcript has minor mis-hearings and shorthand typical of automated transcripts (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" for VPC), speaker labels approximate.
